summary.question: What do you need to know before selling on Amazon?
answers: Amazon is a rigid system, not a flexible storefront like Shopify.
GTINs are permanent identifiers. SKUs are just your internal labels.
Plan the parent-child product tree before you create anything.
Primary images, copy, weights, and packaging details are compliance fields, not decoration.

faqs.question: Is Amazon like Shopify?
faqs.answer: No. Amazon is closer to a rule-based catalog than a customizable store. Edits can be slow, some fields are permanent, and the platform rarely explains what went wrong.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a GTIN and a SKU?
faqs.answer: A GTIN identifies the physical product worldwide and Amazon treats it as permanent. A SKU is your internal tracking code and can be changed. Mixing the two is a common expensive mistake.

faqs.question: Why do parents have to be created before children?
faqs.answer: Amazon’s variation tree is strict. Parent products group the children. Create them in the wrong order and you often have to delete and rebuild, with leftover conflicts in Amazon’s system.

faqs.question: Can I test products and clean them up later?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Amazon remembers GTINs and ASINs even after you delete a listing. Tests can lock identifiers you planned to use on real products.

summary.question: What is a vector file and why do I need one?
answers: Vector files are made of paths, so they scale without going fuzzy.
Logos, print, and signage should live as vectors, not as a PNG from Instagram.
Common formats include SVG, AI, EPS, and PDF.
Printers prefer outlined vectors because they print clean at any size.

faqs.question: Why are vector files important for design?
faqs.answer: They stay sharp at any size. That matters for logos, signs, embroidery, and print, where a JPEG will pixelate.

faqs.question: What are common vector file formats?
faqs.answer: SVG for the web, AI for Adobe Illustrator, EPS as a common exchange format, and PDF when the artwork is saved as vectors rather than a flattened image.

faqs.question: How are vector files different from raster files?
faqs.answer: Raster files (JPG, PNG, GIF) are a grid of pixels. Stretch them and they get blurry. Vectors are math-based paths, so they redraw cleanly at any size.

faqs.question: Can I convert a raster image into a vector?
faqs.answer: You can trace it, but the quality depends on the original. A low-resolution logo screenshot rarely becomes a perfect vector. It is better to redraw it properly.

faqs.question: Do I need special software to open vector files?
faqs.answer: Illustrator, Affinity Designer, or similar tools open AI and EPS files. SVG can open in a browser. Your designer should also send PDF or PNG previews for everyday use.

faqs.question: Why do printers prefer vector files?
faqs.answer: They print at the actual size of the job without losing quality. Outlined text means they do not need your fonts installed.

faqs.question: What is outlined text in a vector file?
faqs.answer: The letters are converted from a live font into shapes. That locks the look for print, but you will need the original file if you want to edit the words later.

faqs.question: Can vector files be used on the web?
faqs.answer: Yes. SVG is the usual web format for logos and simple illustrations. Photos still belong as optimized raster images.

If you want help with SEO or a site built to be found, contact Leanne Digital. We also work on AEO as search shifts toward AI answers.

faqs.question: What is SEO in plain language?
faqs.answer: It is the work of helping search engines understand your site and send the right people to it. Content, technical setup, and links all play a part.

faqs.question: Is SEO the same as my domain name?
faqs.answer: No. The domain is the address. SEO is how people discover that address when they search instead of typing it.

faqs.question: How long does SEO take?
faqs.answer: Longer than a weekend. Like building roads, you see progress over months, not overnight, especially in competitive searches.

faqs.question: Do I still need SEO if I run ads?
faqs.answer: Ads stop when you stop paying. SEO is slower to build and keeps working. Most businesses benefit from both, used on purpose.
